name: CheXBench
intro: CheXBench是用于评估胸部X光图像理解的综合基准，涵盖图像感知、图像-文本推理和文本生成等八种不同任务类型，旨在推动胸部X光AI模型的开发和临床应用。
org: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and Imaging

metric: Accuracy, mIoU/mAP, CheXbert-F1, BERTScore, RadGraph-F1, ROUGE-L
task_type: 多选题, 问答, 文本生成
eval_feature: 胸部X光图像理解, 图像-文本推理, 文本生成，八种任务类型
scale: 三条评测轴, 八类任务；训练背景含32个公开数据集与850万条CheXinstruct三元组
build_method_en: 35-task CXR Taxonomy, Engineering of 32 Public Datasets, Official-split Isolation, Eight-task Evaluation Integration
eval_feature_en: chest X-ray image understanding, image-text reasoning, text generation, eight task types
intro_en: CheXBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating chest X-ray image understanding, covering eight different task types including image perception, image-text reasoning, and text generation. It aims to advance the development and clinical application of chest X-ray AI models.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2401.12208v2, Methods: Description of the CheXinstruct dataset, Building CheXbench, and the reader-study section. The paper defines 35 CXR interpretation tasks, gathers 32 public datasets, and applies manual plus automated engineering to verify quality, unify heterogeneous annotations, restructure reports, and map sources into the task taxonomy. Official source splits are preserved so evaluation cases remain outside model training. This yields two distinct artifacts: CheXinstruct, an 8.5-million instruction-image-response training corpus, and CheXbench, a held-out evaluation benchmark of eight clinically relevant task types organized under image perception, image-text reasoning, and text generation. CheXagent is training context rather than benchmark data: it is trained through clinical-text language-model adaptation, CXR-report vision-encoder learning, and joint instruction tuning, then compared with general and medical foundation models on standardized instructions with one or more images and, where needed, text. Scoring is task-specific, including accuracy, localization metrics, and clinical text-generation metrics. Generated findings also receive radiologist review. A separate eight-radiologist reader study evaluates report drafting/editing time, efficiency, and quality; the diagram keeps those clinical-utility results distinct from CheXbench scores.
